concept:
Character concept for a 2D cut-out animation game. Draw ONE original creature: a sturdy woolly WOOD GOAT with a thicker cream fleece, longer twig horns and a big daisy crown with leaves, the SECOND stage of a three-stage Wood evolution line whose first stage is image 6 (the round goat kid), in the same view and pose as image 1, standing square on four sturdy legs, head facing forward, ready to charge, on a plain white background. A cute, chunky creature, but an original design that must look clearly DIFFERENT from the figure the silhouette came from; not any existing character.

Image 1 (grey silhouette) and image 2 (the same figure split into numbered regions) show the PUPPET RIG the new creature will be animated on. They tell you where each part and joint is, NOT what the creature looks like: do not trace their outline. Viewer-left and viewer-right mean as seen in the picture.

KEEP FROM THE RIG (the animation moves these parts around these joints):
- the same parts, no more, no fewer, each where its numbered region is: 1 face; 2 thick woolly fleece; 3 chest; 4 four legs; 5 two twig horns; 6 big daisy crown; 7 short tail;
- every joint where it is and every part pointing the same way as in image 1; eyes where the old eyes are;
- each part about the size and shape of its region; the whole figure about the same size.

CHANGE (the new look, region by region):
1 face: a round goat face: chestnut brown with a small pale cream muzzle, two big honey-amber eyes (one catchlight dot each) exactly where the old eyes are, brows angled down, a determined small grin with a tiny fang.
2 thick woolly fleece: thick fluffy warm cream wool with soft scalloped curls and the same outline: the back fleece, side tufts, fringe and the two locks beside the face all cream wool; no green, no leaves.
3 chest: a warm cream furry chest, same outline.
4 four legs: four sturdy goat legs with the same outline: cream fur, each ending at the BOTTOM in a dark-brown split hoof.
5 two twig horns: two dark-brown wooden twig horns growing from the same places, longer than the first stage: each a crooked branch sweeping outward and up with one or two short side twigs and small fresh light-green leaf buds; no curls, no tan.
6 big daisy crown: a big crown of five or six yellow daisies with orange-brown centres set in a ring of olive-green leaves, sitting on top of the head in the same place; no stamens, no antennae, no pink.
7 short tail: a short perky goat tail of cream wool with a chestnut-brown tip, sticking up behind the back in the same place.

ATTITUDE: a tough young goat ready to ram: brows angled down, a determined grin with a tiny fang; cute, never scary, never a cheerful mascot.

{RENDER}
{DESIGN}
The style sheet is image 3; the hand-drawn map is image 4. Image 5 is an approved character of this game: copy its ink line weight and its pencil and crayon texture, not its design; it has a few white shine spots and some darker shading: do NOT copy those. Image 6 is the approved first stage of this creature: keep its colours, face and drawing style; this stage is the same creature grown up.

COLOURS: fluffy warm cream wool, a chestnut-brown face with a small pale cream muzzle, dark-brown wooden twig horns with small fresh light-green leaf buds, yellow daisies with orange-brown centres, dark-brown hooves, big honey-amber eyes, olive-green leaves in the crown. Few colours.

AVOID: green or bush-like wool, round curled light-tan ram horns, roses, lilies, pink or pastel-pink flowers, curly yellow-green stamens or antennae, gold armour or gold rings, an all-white or all-cream face, text, labels, numbers, the region colours, frames, background scenery, a second view, shading, shadows, white highlights, glossy shine, glow, gradients.
